title: Constraint-driven validator for region, tier, and fallback model semantics
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: The current routing DSL allows a set of region selectors, tier-based routes, and fallback model variants to be authored separately, but cross-field constraints are weak. We have seen production misroutes when conflicting constraints (region affinity vs capacity tiers) and ambiguous fallback chains (incompatible model variants) slip past unit checks.

Goal: Implement a constraint-driven validation layer that performs both static schema validation and semantic cross-field checks for region selection, tier routing, and fallback model variants. The validator should: enforce deterministic precedence rules, detect incompatible model variant combinations, surface clear human-readable errors with remediation hints, support a compatibility/strip mode for older configs, and be usable both in CI (pre-merge) and at runtime (admission webhook / config load).
acceptance_criteria: New validator integrated into policy compile pipeline and executed in PR CI
All existing e2e policy tests pass under compatibility mode
Validator produces actionable error codes (ERR-RT-01..ERR-RT-12) with remediation suggestions
Runtime loader fails-fast on high-severity semantic violations and emits non-blocking warnings for deprecations
Migration tool (policy-compat-strip) can transform legacy configs to pass the new validator with a single flag
implementation_notes: Introduce a constraint graph representation (directed edges between selectors/variants) to evaluate precedence deterministically
Design validator as a set of independent checkers: syntax, invariants, capacity-affinity, fallback-chain, model-compatibility
Provide a compatibility mode that applies safe rewrites: move region-agnostic routes to explicit locales, expand implicit fallback lists to canonical sequences
Keep checks pure and deterministic so they can run in unit tests and in a lightweight admission path in the private control plane
Expose lint level flags: error / warning / info per rule to allow gradual rollouts
testing_plan: Unit: checker-specific fuzz tests (randomized region + tier + fallback trees) to assert no panics and proper rule classification
Integration: compile+simulate end-to-end policy dispatch across 3 simulated regions and 2 capacity tiers
Regression: run full policy suite from production fixtures under compatibility mode and strict mode
Canary: deploy validator in readonly mode on staging config loader for 48h to capture real-world false positives
Performance: measure validation latency on large (10k-rule) policies; target median < 40ms per policy
progress_updates: 2025-02-19 - Discovery: surveyed current rule authoring patterns; found 4 common anti-patterns causing ambiguous region fallthroughs (notes in Confluence)
2025-02-24 - Design: RFC merged with constraint graph approach and rule taxonomy (contrib: Elena Torres, Priya Shah) https://confluence.redwood.ai/policy-validator-rfc

2025-02-28 - Spike: prototype checker implemented in rust-policy-lib; initial unit tests added (branch: feat/constraint-validator-spike) https://github.com/redwood-inference/policy/compare/feat/constraint-validator-spike
2025-03-03 - Review: architecture review meeting with runtime and console teams; agreed on error code schema and backward-compat flag semantics
2025-03-04 - Implementation: started migration CLI (policy-compat-strip) and added compatibility-mode path to compiler; ongoing work to add model-compatibility matrix
open_questions: How strict should capacity-affinity checks be by default for Dedicated customers who rely on soft fallbacks?
Should runtime loader allow configurable per-tenant lint thresholds (e.g., errors treated as warnings for early-stage accounts)?
Where to persist validation issue telemetry (Console events vs. central policy-audit service)?
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: strict validator may block valid legacy configs -> Mitigation: compatibility mode + migration CLI + staged rollout
Risk: validator adds startup latency for large fleets -> Mitigation: compile-on-change caching and asynchronous background revalidation
Risk: false positives on model-compatibility -> Mitigation: maintain model variant compatibility matrix and a fallback allowlist; ship rollback toggle
